title: Machine learning for host-pathogen protein-protein interaction prediction: A tutorial paper
content:
by Jerry Emmanuel, Itunu Babatunmise, Jelili Oyelade

The study of Host-Pathogen Protein-Protein Interactions (HP-PPIs) is critical for understanding mechanisms of infectious disease and for the development of therapeutic interventions. Computational prediction of HP-PPIs has become essential due to the limitations of experimental approaches, which are labour-intensive and expensive. In this tutorial, we present a step-by-step machine learning pipeline for HP-PPI prediction implemented in Google Colab. The workflow consists of six stages implemented in six Google Colab notebooks: dataset preparation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, machine learning model training, hyperparameter tuning and validation and model deployment. Six widely used classifiers, including LightGBM, Multi-layer Perceptron, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were evaluated using balanced and imbalanced datasets from human-bacteria protein interactions. Amino acid composition was evaluated as a standalone feature descriptor, while pseudo amino acid and conjoint triad descriptors were concatenated into a second feature set. Among the classifiers, LightGBM achieved the highest mean cross-validation performance Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) and was subsequently selected for evaluation on an independent test set. Leave-One-Pathogen-Out validation was additionally performed to assess the ability of the selected model to generalise to unseen bacterial pathogens. This tutorial provides a reproducible and adaptable framework for HP-PPI prediction that can be extended to other pathogen systems. It is beginner-friendly and provides a starting point for researchers with limited computational backgrounds exploring the research domain of infectious disease biology.
